taxonomic_note: Accepted by Kew/POWO; native in Texas. Historical synonyms include Poa trichodes, Eragrostis pilifera, and E. trichodes var. pilifera.
look_here_first: SAND LOVEGRASS: larger arching perennial bunch with a spacious sometimes oblong fountain of very thin panicle branches bearing small pale spikelets toward branch tips. Real archived photos show a whole tuft and scale-reference tiny separate spikelets. On fresh sheaths, longer hairs often concentrate at sheath THROAT/collar (hair fringe ligule), while nodes tend smooth; this critical collar is NOT in current photos. Compare plains and bigtop by actual sheath hair location and ripe spikelets.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays County regional report lists sand lovegrass among natural grasses found in the Hays County study area. UT Plant Resources Center has a Williamson County field treatment. Kerr Wildlife Management Area vascular checklist includes Eragrostis trichodes.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Candidate seed mixes were not counted as native-county evidence.

best_field_traits: long hairs concentrated at sheath throat/collar
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Eragrostis intermedia: Usually shorter with mostly smooth sheaths and a smaller airy panicle. Eragrostis hirsuta: Hirsute across sheath surface with bearded panicle axils rather than collar-focused long hairs. Eragrostis cilianensis: Annual, coarser, glandular and many-flowered.
crew_field_walkthrough: SAND LOVEGRASS: larger arching perennial bunch with a spacious sometimes oblong fountain of very thin panicle branches bearing small pale spikelets toward branch tips. Real archived photos show a whole tuft and scale-reference tiny separate spikelets. On fresh sheaths, longer hairs often concentrate at sheath THROAT/collar (hair fringe ligule), while nodes tend smooth; this critical collar is NOT in current photos. Compare plains and bigtop by actual sheath hair location and ripe spikelets.
On the SAME mature plant, compare full sheath-body hair distribution versus throat, then actual lower branch-axil and mature spikelet with scale.
If photo lacks collar and true spikelet characters, teach genus-level ID and mark the remaining photo tasks.
morphology_keys.what_to_teach_crew: SAND = BIG open panicle, throat hairs; look for fine dangling branches carrying small spikelets. The plant can look like a transparent fountain. To confirm, check hair LOCATION (throat not sheath-wide) and the mature spikelets.
overlap_cautions: The small visible spikelets and pedicels help teach panicle parts but do not distinguish the species on their own.
The existing canonical finger-scale reproductive image does NOT depict the ligule or sheath-throat hairs; do not put an arrow claiming it does.
E. intermedia also has a very open inflorescence and throat hairs; collect comparative sheath and complete-head photographs.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: True collar throat hairs and ligule with mm scale
Ripe 6–10 flowered spikelets with glume attachments at 10–20×

comparisons.key_distinctions: Sand lovegrass combines a relatively tall persistent tuft, arching foliage and a large airy oblong panicle with throat-focused long hairs. Plains lovegrass is often shorter with less shaggy sheath body and a smaller panicle; bigtop typically bears more extensive sheath hairiness. Stinkgrass is an annual with coarser glandular reproductive parts. None of these is guaranteed from a lone distant view.

measured_diagnostic_key_20261022.look_here_first: Large arching perennial bunchgrass with fine open panicle; confirm actual collar hair arrangement and mature spikelet.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261022.measured_diagnostic: UT Williamson treatment: ligule around 0.4 mm, sheath-throat hairs to 4–5 mm; glumes around 1.5–3 mm, three-veined lemma around 2.6–3.2 mm; awns absent. Regional floret counts vary.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261022.local_lookalikes: E. intermedia and E. hirsuta require sheath and spikelet comparison; E. spectabilis has broader tumbling panicle.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261022.last_mile_photo_arrow_gaps: Rooted tuft, same-plant ligule versus long sheath-throat hairs, 10–20× dissected spikelet with ruler, and matched lovegrass sheath views.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261022.public_ready_criteria: Retain existing taxonomy holds, source/photo/license and annotation records. Require taxon-verified measured diagnostic photographs, individual public-use rights and pixel-accurate arrow plus site QA before FINISHED.

critical_gaps: Short 0.4-mm true hair-fringe ligule vs 4-5-mm long oral/collar hairs

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Sand lovegrass: don't stop at the giant cloud
steps: Photograph the full mature head and the rooted tuft together.
Look up-close for a pale spikelet at the tip of a fine branch.
Locate the throat/collar hairs on a different frame — they are NOT pictured in the spikelet macro.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Use size/architecture to find the candidate; do not finalize without collar anatomy and mature spikelets.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: The original three photographed species images now include the USDA-NRCS Texas Plant Materials Center public-domain overview (if archive succeeded) and two field views. Public-domain broad habit is not evidence for true 0.4-mm ligule fringe or lower glume. Need 10-20× collar and spikelet dissection with physical ruler.
